title: One step RT-ddPCR for probes to target eRNA samples
author: Marine Vautier
materials: Equipment decontamination: - Specific DNA-workstation: UV decontamination. Turn on the following equipments: - the QX200 droplet generator - the PX1 PCR plate sealer at 180 °C - the thermal cycler for PCR - the QX600 or QX200 droplet reader for ddPCR Tubes annotation - One 0.5 mL / 1.5 mL / 2 mL or 5 mL tube for the reaction mix according to the number of samples to be analysed. - PCR strips: 8 samples per PCR strip.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Reaction Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the reaction mix on ice under a specific DNA/RNA-workstation, covering photosensitive reagents with aluminium foil.

substeps.instruction: Calculate reagent requirements based on the number of samples (Table 2).
Thaw all reagents on ice for 30 minutes.
Vortex each tube thoroughly for 30 seconds and centrifuge briefly.
Add reagents to the tube one by one to prepare the reaction mix.
Vortex and centrifuge the reaction mix briefly.
Cover the reaction mix tube with aluminium foil; store at room temperature for immediate use or on ice for later use.

steps.title: Distribute Mix and RNA Samples
steps.instruction: Distribute the reaction mix and RNA samples into PCR strips on ice.

substeps.instruction: Defrost negative/positive controls and RNA samples on ice for 10 minutes; use DNase and RNase free water for NTC.
Pipet the reaction mix into each PCR strip well (e.g., 20 µL of mix if 2 µL of RNA is selected).
Vortex and centrifuge each RNA and control sample briefly.
Add the specified quantity of RNA samples and controls into the corresponding PCR strip wells according to the plate layout.
Close and annotate the PCR strips, then cover them with aluminium foil.
Vortex PCR strips at maximum speed for 10 seconds and centrifuge briefly.
Equilibrate strips to room temperature for no more than 10 minutes before droplet generation (otherwise keep on ice).

steps.title: Generate Droplets
steps.instruction: Generate droplets using a DG8 cartridge and droplet generator. This step must follow the previous distribution step in less than one hour.

substeps.instruction: Vortex and centrifuge all PCR strips.
Place a DG8 cartridge into the holder and dispense 20 µL of the RNA sample + reaction mix into the middle line and 70 µL of droplet generation oil into the bottom line.
Ensure all 8 samples are filled (no empty wells) and avoid bubbles by tilting the pipette at 15° and dispensing gently without pushing the plunger after the first stop.
Place a DG8 gasket for ddPCR on the cartridge.
Insert the cartridge into the droplet generator and start the generation process.
Remove the cartridge and gasket once the three indicator lights turn green.

steps.title: Transfer Droplets and Seal Plate
steps.instruction: Transfer generated droplets to a 96-well plate and seal.

substeps.instruction: Using a multi-channel pipet, slowly transfer 40 µL of droplets from the top line of the cartridge into the ddPCR 96-well plate.
Intake: Place tips at the bottom of the well at a 30-45° angle and draw 40 µL slowly (approx. 5 seconds).
Dispense: Position tip along the side of the well (not at the bottom) and dispense slowly (approx. 5 seconds).
Cover and store the plate on ice until all samples are loaded.
Seal the plate with a pierceable foil seal (colored line on top) at 180 °C for 5 seconds using a PCR plate sealer.
Verify all wells are sealed.

steps.title: Perform Thermal Cycling
steps.instruction: Run the PCR thermal cycling program.

substeps.instruction: Begin thermal cycling within 30 minutes of sealing, or store at 4 °C for up to 4 hours.
Place the sealed plate into the PCR thermal cycler and program the cycling conditions (Table 3).
Start the PCR run.
Store the plate for up to 24 hours if not reading immediately.

steps.title: Read Droplets and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Read the plate using a QX200 or QX600 droplet reader and analyze results via software.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the reader, place the plate in the support, and insert it into the machine.
Open the associated software and check oil and waste bin levels (prime if new oil is installed; flush system if unused for >1 month).
Define the experiment in the software: Add/configure plate, select wells to be analyzed, and optionally enter well information (target, channel, sample type).
Click 'Start Run' and monitor results live or view them in the dedicated folder after completion.
